paper.title: PlanRAG-Audio: Planning and Retrieval Augmented Generation for Long-form Audio Understanding

latest_version.version_label: Findings of ACL 2026 camera-ready, reviewed on 2026-08-31

evidence.paraphrase: The paper constructs a reproducible evaluation suite from public audio corpora rather than merely reporting results on unchanged source datasets. Base tasks cover long-form QA, summarization, diarization, emotion recognition and sound-event detection; inputs span 10, 30, 60, 300 and 540 minutes, with 1,000 questions per task except 100 summaries.

Advanced evaluation sets transform the base data into speaker counting, sound-event ordering and speaker-constrained QA. Speaker-constrained QA includes answerable and deliberately unanswerable cases, while event ordering and counting require evidence integration across long time spans and modality-specific streams.

adjudication_notes: Recorded separately from the PlanRAG-Audio architecture because the paper contributes both a memory architecture and a newly constructed multi-task evaluation suite.
The authors do not give the suite a separate benchmark brand; 'PlanRAG-Audio evaluation' follows the manuscript Table 1 label and the corpus precedent for named evaluation records.

Classified as memory_adjacent because it stresses retrieval and reasoning over retained long-form audio, but primarily evaluates long-audio understanding rather than isolating a persistent agent-memory lifecycle.
